reflections.title: "The LORD Is My Shepherd; I Shall Not Want"

reflect.text: Daily life often brings heavy duties and endless hurry. When we try to manage everything by relying on our own strength, we quickly become worn out and empty. Our hearts get noisy and cluttered with worry. We may look to worldly success, money, or other people to refresh us, but these things can never bring true rest to an exhausted soul.

Jesus steps in as our Good Shepherd to care for us completely. He knows when our pace has become relentless, and He lovingly makes us pause to rest beside quiet waters. As Scotty Smith highlights, Christ gives us an inner spiritual quietness that calms our restless spirits. He replenishes our strength and restores balance to our lives.

Our Shepherd also leads us forward along grace-filled paths that bring honor to His name. Instead of carrying tomorrow's burdens on our own shoulders, we can trust His gentle direction and find peace tonight in His faithful care.

questions: What responsibilities or worries are leaving you feeling depleted right now?
How can you pause today and let Jesus restore quietness to your heart?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being my Shepherd who sees when I am weary and running low. Calm my noisy heart with Your peace, and restore my soul. Help me to stop relying on myself so I can follow Your right paths today. Amen.

D5.work: Shepherded by Jesus – Praying through Psalm 23 – Pt. 1

reflections.title: "Even Though I Walk Through the Valley of the Shadow of Death"

reflect.text: We often hear this verse read at the close of life, but it speaks just as powerfully to our daily struggles. Many believers walk through dark seasons of depression, sorrow, or frightening thoughts. In these deep valleys, our spirits can feel pressed down and overwhelmed, as if darkness is closing in on every side.

Yet even in those terrifying moments, the Lord is right beside us. His presence keeps us from receiving any deadly spiritual harm. Charles Spurgeon wrote that the Holy Spirit can make a Christian "independent of outward circumstances." When the world around us shakes, God gives us an inner light that darkness cannot put out.

Neither failing health nor poverty can take away this comfort. Even if our bodies suffer pain or our strength fades, Jesus becomes our brightest guide and sweetest song. Because our Shepherd walks with us, we can meet every dark valley with quiet confidence instead of fear.

questions: What dark valley or heavy sadness feels overwhelming to you today?
How does remembering that Jesus walks beside you bring peace to your fears?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You that I never walk through dark and scary places alone. When my spirit feels heavy with sadness or weakness, shine Your light deep within me. Keep me safe with Your rod and staff, and give me a calm trust in Your constant care. Amen.

reflections.title: Goodness and Mercy All Our Days

reflect.text: When we look at Psalm 23 as a whole, we see God's faithful care surrounding our entire journey. Charles Spurgeon pictured goodness and mercy as "two guards" that follow us closely wherever we go. Every single day of our lives, from the ordinary to the unusual, is guarded by these two companions sent by the Lord.

These companions have distinct roles in our lives. God's goodness attends our steps to supply all our daily needs, while His mercy reaches out to forgive and wash away our sins. Together, they bring up the rear and protect us until our earthly journey ends and we dwell with God forever.

Knowing that goodness and mercy follow us prompts a glad response. We can praise God with genuine joy and offer our hearts fully to Him. When we are confident of His unfailing care, we are freed to show creative love to others and give generously to those in need.

questions: How have you seen God's goodness meet your needs and His mercy forgive your sins recently?
What is one practical way you can show generous love to someone in need today?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for sending Your goodness to provide for me and Your mercy to pardon my sins. Help me to remember that these two blessings follow me every day of my life. Teach me to serve You with joy and share Your generous love with others. Amen.
